# agent-video

Watch a video as frame grids: timestamped JPEG canvases a VLM can read
directly, with subtitles and key-frame metadata riding along.

## MCP path (preferred)

If the host supports MCP servers, register the stdio server and call the
`video` tool — grid images arrive directly in context:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "video": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@agent-video/cli", "mcp"] } } }
```

Protocol — the response always tells you what to do next:

1. Call with only `source`. Local video file path or URL. Call with only `source` first; the response tells you what to do next.
2. `"status": "plan"` — probe summary plus `recommended_calls`; copy one
   argument object verbatim into the next call.
3. `"status": "confirm_required"` — the action needs explicit consent.
   Echo a consent token issued by a previous response to authorize the pending action. Tokens are single-use and bound to the latest plan; pass confirm alone with source.
4. `"status": "pending"` — a background download is running; repeat the
   same call to poll.
5. `"status": "ready"` — grid images plus one text block carrying time
   ranges, key frames, subtitles, and notices.

Refining parameters:

- `from` — Window start: seconds (83) or timestamp ("1:23", "1:02:03"). Omit to start from the beginning.
- `until` — Window end, same formats. Omit to go to the end of the video.
- `look` — How to look: overview (fast triage), detailed (miss nothing), read_text (few large frames to read on-screen text/UI), track_motion (dense small frames for fast action). Subtitle text always rides along in metadata regardless; this only affects frame size/density. Omit for a balanced default.
- `raw` — Expert escape hatch: verbatim agent-video core CLI arguments starting with the subcommand, e.g. "process --strategy keyframes --base-fps 0.2". Mutually exclusive with from/until/look/strategy. Input/output plumbing is injected by the server.

## Bash path (no MCP client)

Run the CLI, then open the produced grid JPEGs with the host's file/image
reader:

```sh
npx -y @agent-video/cli process video.mp4 -o out/
```

- `out/` receives the grid JPEGs plus `metadata.json`: per-grid time
  ranges, key frames, and subtitle text.
- Single dense grid of a short range:
  `npx -y @agent-video/cli extract video.mp4 --range 01:23-01:35 -o out/`
- Sampling/strategy flags: `npx -y @agent-video/cli process --help`.

## URLs

On the MCP path, pass the URL as `source` — download and consent are
handled by the server. On the bash path, fetch the file yourself first
(e.g. yt-dlp) and pass the local path.
